newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices decline again led by merino wool.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices decline again led by merino wool.

text.p: Wool prices declined again at Napier and Christchurch wool sales on Thursday with merino wools leading the decline, Wools of New Zealand.
The provisional market indicators moved as follows:
- strong segment down five cents to $4.12
- lamb segment down seven cents to $4.49
Some 16 percent of the 3,717 tonnes on offer was passed in. Dominating the offering was 34 percent crossbred fleece, 21 percent second shear and 17 percent merino fleece.
Against last week's sales, merino 17 micron was 10-15 percent cheaper, 18-20 micron 5-7 percent cheaper, 21-22 micron 2.5-5 percent cheaper and 23 micron 1 percent dearer.
Halfbred and crossbred fleece was up to 1 percent cheaper, second sheear was up to 1.5 percent cheaper and first lambs bulky skirtings and second shear bellies and bellies were generally unchanged.
Main interest came from Western Europe, China and local mills with support from India, Japan and Nepal.
The next sales are at Napier and Christchurch on December 5.
